summary: Argues benchmarking is a surrogate measure and prospective clinical studies with patient outcomes should be the main evidence for devices that influence patient care.
Emergency physician and small DGBI app maker supports the framework but urges counterfactual comparators, trajectory envelopes, presumptive evidence tiers, and size-scaled third-party fees.
Objects that emergency room AI captures and indexes patient voice prints without informed consent, violating HIPAA, HITECH, and wiretapping laws.
Using IDx-DR and a vignette experiment, argues the workflow position of AI output relative to clinician assessment must be fixed in intended use for team evaluation.
Answers all 26 questions, arguing capability does not confer authority and proposing risk modifiers, a reconstructable event record, and governed reliance and execution for agents.

org: The Christman AI Project / Luma Cognify AI
summary: Argues periodic re-benchmarking misses within-session degradation and proposes continuous claim-versus-independent-record verification with alerts to caregivers of nonverbal users.
Prototype builder reports multi-turn failure modes and asks for case-locked history completeness scoring, replay consistency, instruction-lock tests, and re-testing after model changes.
Experiment shows multimodal LLMs diagnose without the image depending on demographics, so benchmarks must test missing inputs and abstention across all output channels.
Says deploying institutions must be able to inventory, permission, log, and stop GenAI devices, and FDA should require manufacturers to enable these capabilities.
Reimbursement consultancy supports the competency framework but calls for a pathway decision matrix, FDA-CMS coverage alignment, PCCP change categories, and small-business support.
Proposes treating the full system configuration as the unit of assurance, with an auditable lifecycle assurance case, AI-SBOM, deterministic safety controls, and bounded agent authority.

Regulatory affairs professional answers all questions, urging a detectability axis, published evidence mapping, invariant-based PCCPs, version pinning as a design control, and independent supervisors.

org: Nurse Deb Speaking, Media & Consulting, LLC
summary: Nurse advocate warns patient-facing and administrative agents can miss latent clinical needs, urging evidence-grounded triage, outcome monitoring, and oversight of non-device healthcare AI.
Supports competency evaluation and proposes competency envelopes, trajectory stress testing, non-compensable safety floors, public competency profiles, and impact-based requalification.
Emergency physician urges that agentic devices produce tamper-evident proof a present human authorized each consequential action, scaled by reversibility and consequence.

Software engineer recommends enforced authorization for agent actions, decision-linked monitoring, rehearsed interventions, impact-based change assessment, supplier fallback plans, and protected investigation records.
